hints: Notice the graph starts at $v = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, crosses zero at $t = 2.0 \text{ s}$, and reaches $v = -10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$.
Recall that displacement is the signed area under a velocity-time graph, with area above the $t$-axis positive and area below negative.
Calculate the triangle above the axis from $0$ to $2.0 \text{ s}$ and subtract the smaller triangle below the axis from $2.0 \text{ s}$ to $3.0 \text{ s}$.
walkthrough: Read the $v$-$t$ graph: at $t = 0$, $v = +20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upwards, at $t = 2.0 \text{ s}$, $v = 0$, and at $t = 3.0 \text{ s}$, $v = -10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ downwards.
Use the rule that displacement $= $ area under the $v$-$t$ graph, taking area above the time axis as positive and below as negative.
Upward displacement from $0$ to $2.0 \text{ s}$ is the upper triangle: $A_{up} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2.0 \text{ s} \times 20 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 20 \text{ m}$.

Downward displacement from $2.0 \text{ s}$ to $3.0 \text{ s}$ is the lower triangle of base $1.0 \text{ s}$ and height $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $A_{down} = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.0 \text{ s} \times 10 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 5 \text{ m}$.
Net displacement from X is $s = A_{up} - A_{down} = 20 \text{ m} - 5 \text{ m} = 15 \text{ m}$.
Positive means still above the starting point X, so $15 \text{ m}$ above X. This is option A.
